title: Email Campaign Executive
description:
Ready to make your mark in digital marketing?

If you love getting stuck into email campaigns, spotting what makes a subject line work, and turning data into decisions, this could be your next big move.

An exciting opportunity has opened up for an Email Campaign Executive to join a well-established manufacturer in the safety equipment sector, based in Oxfordshire. This is a genuinely international business, and this role puts you right at the centre of how they communicate with their global distribution network.

You'll take ownership of email marketing campaigns from planning through to reporting, working closely with Product, Sales and Marketing teams across multiple regions. It's a role with real variety, real responsibility, and real opportunity to grow.

On offer is a salary of £27,000 plus a bonus of up to £2,000 a year, paid quarterly based on sales targets. You'll also get 25 days holiday, an employer-matched pension, a personal development plan, Perkbox discounts, a wellbeing programme, and a cycle-to-work scheme. The role is office-based (with WFH one day a week once you're through probation), so you'll need your own transport to get there.

Key Responsibilities:
- Plan, build and send email campaigns for the company's global distribution network
- Manage a global campaign calendar so every send lands on time
- Build targeted campaigns around customer needs and business goals
- Create and manage automated journeys, nurture campaigns and lead generation
- Work closely with Product, Sales and Marketing teams across different regions
- Keep the marketing database clean and GDPR-compliant
- Run A/B tests to keep improving campaign performance
- Track KPIs and turn the numbers into clear, actionable insight
- Make sure every campaign matches company brand guidelines and technical accuracy
- Support event promotion and follow-up lead nurturing
- Spot opportunities to improve automation, reporting and campaign efficiency

Skills & Experience:
- 2+ years' experience in email marketing, campaign management or marketing automation
- Experience in a B2 B marketing environment
- Confident with CRM systems and customer data
- Hands-on experience with email marketing platforms and automation tools
- Comfortable analysing performance data and turning it into recommendations
- Experience building campaign reports and dashboards
- Sharp attention to detail and solid project management skills
- Strong written communication and copywriting ability
- Able to juggle multiple campaigns and deadlines at once
- A team player who's used to working across marketing, sales and product
- Bonus points for experience with international markets or multi-language campaigns

How to Apply:

This is a genuine chance to grow your marketing career inside an established, international manufacturer, with training, support and real ownership from day one. If you're re ady to take the next step, apply now or contact Niche Recruitment with any questions.

title: Marketing Executive
description:
Marketing Executive

Oxfordshire

£30-40k

VR/10568

A fantastic opportunity has arisen for a skilled Marketing Executive to join a successful and well-established company based in Oxfordshire, who are part of a large international group. They are now embarking on an exciting phase of growth and this is a new role to help increase their impact and reach.

This role is perfect for an all round marketer who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys building from the ground up.

Reporting to the Marketing Manager, the Marketing Executive will primarily focus on D2 C and B2 B funnels optimisation. Your work will directly contribute to brand awareness, lead generation, and revenue growth.

Your role will involve:
- Brand - Keep consistency within the company's core brand values, tone, and visual identity across all customer-facing assets (website, social media, email, print, etc.).
- Campaigns and Email Marketing - Develop, execute, and optimise multi-channel campaigns (email, social, paid, organic) to drive conversion.
- A/B test subject lines, CTAs, and content to refine performance.
- SEO, Content and Design - Create and optimise landing pages, blog posts,and marketing collateral.
- Conduct keyword research and implement on-page SEO best practices (meta tags, headers, internal linking) to improve organic search rankings.
- Design on marketing materials (social posts,brochures, presentations) using brand guidelines
- Social media - Manage and grow the company's presence on LinkedIn (B2 B) and Instagram (D2 C and B2 B), tailoring content for each audience.
- Events - Coordinate with event partners to ensure seamless execution of conferences and planned activities
- CRM - Maintain data hygiene in the CRM (e.g., deduplication, missing information, tagging)
- Performance Marketing - Collect, visualise, and interpret performance data to inform decisions.

You will be the ideal candidate due to your:
- Previous marketing experience in B2 C and/or B2 B.
- Marketing generalist mindset: Comfortable wearing multiple hats and adapting to evolving priorities
- Strong content marketing and storytelling skills: Ability to craft SEO-optimised narratives for diverse audiences.
- Data-driven decision-making: Proficient in analysing metrics (GA4, CRM reports and more) to optimise campaigns.
- Proactive and autonomous.
- Growth mindset: Curious, resourceful, and always seeking to learn and improve.
- Hands-on CRM experience.

Desirable
- HubSpot knowledge and/or certification
- Canva or designing tools (Adobe Suite, Figma)
- Brevo or other email marketing tools
- E-commerce platform i.e Shopify
- SEO/SEM knowledge: Basic understanding of technical SEO, backlinking, and paid search strategies
- Project Management: Ability to juggle multiple deadlines.

title: Temporary Administrator
description:
Berry Recruitment are NOW hiring for a for a Temporary Administrator for our client based in Oxford. The Office Administrator is required to prioritise work throughout the day, ready to change to a different task in response to new needs/requests arising.

The Benefits on offer
Role: Administrator
Location: Oxford, Oxfordshire
Hours - Monday - Friday - 08:00 - 17:00
Salary: £12.71 Per hour

To provide administrative support to the Office Manager in the day-to-day running of the office and to carry out your own dedicated administration tasks and customer care. The Office Administrator is required to prioritise work throughout the day, ready to change to a different task in response to new needs/requests arising.

About the role:
As a Temporary Administrator your duties will be:
- To become familiar with all systems and office procedures with a focus on raising our paper and/or electronic Logbooks for recording site visits.
- To work collaboratively within the Office team in the provision of effective administrative work.
- To undertake wider agreed tasks that support the organisation and your own professional development.

About you:
- Good Administrative skills with an excellent eye for detail and accuracy.
- A sound working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
- Good verbal and written communication skills, including a professional telephone and e-mail manner.
- Ability to meet deadlines and prioritise tasks.
- Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information.
- Effective team player.
- Able to self-motivate, prioritise, plan and organise, including when under pressure.
- Have a proactive approach, taking responsibility for actions and consequences.
- A flexible approach to working with a 'can do' attitude.

No candidate will meet every single desired qualification we have listed. If your experience looks a little different but you think you can bring value to the role, we'd love to learn more about you!"

For more information and to apply, contact the Oxford branch of Berry Recruitment - or click 'Apply Now' to submit your application.

We are committed to fair and inclusive recruitment. All applicants will be considered on the basis of their skills, experience, qualifications and ability to perform the role, and no applicant will be treated less favourably because of a protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010.

title: Administrator
description: To provide efficient administrative support to the CYP0-19 Public Health Service for the children, young people and families ,supporting the implementation of the Healthy Child Programme . The post holder will be the main point of contact for the administration of appointments within the CYP 0-19 years service for parents/carers and young people of Oxfordshire. The post holder will work within the team in our SPA(Single Point of Access). To provide comprehensive timely administrative support to our Children and Young People Public Health Service, incorporating Health Visiting, School Health Nursing and Family Nurse Partnership. Managing databases ,using Microsoft platforms ,Excel and updating information on Electronic Health Records. Prioritise work accordingly ,following the CYP 0-19 Public Health Service Standard Operating Procedures (SOPS). Responding to the needs of service and the clients in a timely manner. Perform general office duties, including responding to emails and phone enquiries appropriately following Trust procedures. Be able to work independently, proactively and as part of a team. Standard Operating Proceedures. JOB PURPOSE To provide efficient administrative support to the 0-19 CYP Public Health Service for the children, young people, and families, supporting the implementation of the 0-19 Healthy Child Programme (HCP) Accurately inputting data and maintaining database information systems. This includes collating information from partner services and organisations. The post holder will be the main point of contact for the administration of appointments within the 0-19 CYP Public Health Service for parent/carers and young people, in Oxfordshire. The Post Holder will work as part of the Single Point of access (SPA). When appropriate hold a ChatHealth Licence to provide administrative support to the practitioners working on the platform. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Clinical responsibilities: To provide comprehensive, timely administrative support to the 0-19 CYP Public Health Service. Working within a Single Point of Access (SPA). databases and Microsoft Office Responsible for accurately inputting, correcting, and closing patient information on their Electronic Health Records (EHR), using relevant clinical applications. Ensuring that all referrals received are tracked through to team allocation and any problems are resolved. Prioritise workload, accordingly, following the 0-19 CYP Public Health Service , Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and policies, responding to the needs of service and the clients in a timely manner. Have good organisational abilities, to be able to manage own workload and contribute to the organisation of the relevant team. Communicate politely and effectively with clients, healthcare staff, and others, courteously and responsively. Establish and maintain clinician and clinic diaries, arranging meetings, making appointments, and resolving diary conflicts. Scheduling and re-arranging diary entries, ensuring accurate record keeping and outcoming of appointments. To perform general office duties including responding to email and phone enquiries. Answering the telephone, taking, and recording messages accurately, responding to queries appropriately, following Trust procedures and protocols and organise the maintenance of the electronic filing systems for the relevant team. Taking and producing accurate meeting minutes and follow up any actions arising. To maintain service supplies: order, check, maintain and distribute equipment and supplies for the team as required. Then receipt orders. Undertake photocopying and scanning as required. Contacting the Estates or Facilities Department to carry out repairs, checking work has been undertaken to satisfaction. Provide cover for other team members and provide cross cover within the directorate and across the Trust as required. To provide feedback to 0-19 CYP Public Health Service managers to improve ways of working within the team and to assist managers in the development, testing and implementation of new IT, telephony, and information systems. escalating to line manager/LTL any concerns with undertaking any tasks. Band: 3 Criteria for Selection Essential Requirements Desirable Requirements Knowledge Requirements Good general level of education Previous experience in administrative role Previous experience in NHS Business administration BTEC Qualifications/Academic/Skills/ Professional GSCE pass in Maths & English Qualification at NVQ Level 2 or equivalent NVQ2 in business administration or equivalent or office/administration experience ECDL (European Computer Driving License) or equivalent experience Further training or job-related aptitude and skills Motivated and enthusiastic Competent in using various Microsoft Office applications. Understands and adheres to the need for confidentiality. Interpersonal skills, face to face and telephone Ability to accurately maintain records and electronic filing systems. Able to plan own workload and prioritise work of several managers following local policy Aptitude to take and transcribe minutes. Good communication skills written and verbal Ability and willingness to attend training away from the workplace Ability and willingness to travel between community team locations independently, as required by the organisation Ability to rotate job base as needs of service require Ability to work autonomously and as part of a team to deliver team objective Proactive approach Ability to problem solve and prioritise Experience in use of other databases/IT systems Experience Experience of working in a Team Microsoft Office skills Experience of dealing with Service Users Experience of diary management Experience of working in a health- related or educational environment Personal Qualities Good communication skills written & verbal. Accurate attention to detail Demonstrates a non-judgmental approach. Excellent interpersonal skills Flexible towards needs of team and service with a willingness to adapt to necessary change Empathic and respect for the rights and needs of others Commitment to service users and the team, and the wider Trust to improve the service given as necessary Contractual or other requirements Ability to travel across a defined location independently, as required by the organisation

title: Administrator
description: Are you looking for a new office based challenge working for a hardworking enthusiastic and vibrant mental health service? Would you like to be part of a well functioning team which values the wellbeing of all members of the team and prides itself on being a team people want people want to work for? We are seeking a part time Administrator to join the team! Based within the Oxfordshire Early Intervention Service (OEIS) office, the post holder will undertake a range of day to day administrative duties including managing records, processing referrals, coordinating meetings, maintaining electronic systems, and supporting communication across the team. We would love to hear from you should this exciting role appeal to you. Please contact Cynthia Wakonyo (Performance & Administration Manager) if you have any questions regarding this post. Be responsible for providing an efficient administrative/secretarial service to the OEIS team Be a contact and channel of communication between users of the service and the team, maintaining a professional but sympathetic manner. Taking minutes of meetings. Deal appropriately with sensitive and confidential information from the clinical team using initiative to direct appropriately. Provide reception cover Provide ad hoc, flexible, and focussed admin support to the team as required, ensuring that the office is stocked with relevant forms and stationery to ensure a smooth-running office. We hope that the advert has given you a clear understanding of the skills we are seeking and the opportunity at hand. You will need to use the supporting statement element of your application form to demonstrate your suitability for this role and you should refer to the job description, person specification and the guidance notes attached to this role to help you tailor your application. The essential and desirable criteria will be used to shortlist for interview, and you should ensure that you refer to these within your application to increase your chances of being selected for interview.

title: Forensic Administrator - Littlemore, Oxford
description: We are looking for an excellent Administrator to join our admin team at Oxford Clinic, Littlemore Mental Health Centre in Oxford. You will work with senior members of the multidisciplinary team to provide direct administrative support. We are looking for an enthusiastic, flexible, empathetic and self-motivated individual to work within our team. Please note the interview is face to face and will contain a minute taking exercise. The successful candidate will need to have proven administrative experience with a good eye for detail, excellent communication, administrative and organisational / prioritisation skills, knowledge of Microsoft Office, Word, Excel, managing Outlook diaries, and minute taking and will be able to liaise with employees at all levels. They will also have the skills to handle all contacts confidently with compassion, patience and professionalism. The role will suit someone who enjoys being busy, where they would be able to work as a part of a team, as well as using their own initiative. This is an important role which helps run an efficient service but is also an extremely rewarding one. We will offer the successful candidate a supportive team, with regular supervision meetings, opportunities for continued professional development and a friendly and sometimes challenging working environment. We are looking for an individual with Experience of working within an administrative role Good communication skills Good written and verbal skills Experience of servicing meetings including minute taking. Word processing experience with audio and copy typing The ability to work under pressure Ability to prioritise own workload An understanding of GDPR and the Data Protection Act A commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. Knowledge of Microsoft Office packages including Microsoft Teams
